answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using hardware enclave attestation. Agents execute inside secure processors, routing signed proofs across an attestation bridge to mint identities. This verification knoll prevents bots from multiplying like yarrow across cloud servers, forcing attackers to incur verifiable capital costs in physical silicon per identity. However, microarchitectural side-channel leaks can expose root keys, allowing adversaries to forge valid credentials.
